Create a file named case_120.inp in the working directory containing exactly the input deck provided, preserving all formatting, node coordinates, element connectivity, boundary conditions, material definition, NSETs, the *TRANSFORM definition, and the empty *STEP / *END STEP as given, without adding, removing, or modifying any physics-related lines.
Run CalculiX using the command ccx -i case_120, falling back to ccx case_120 if the -i form is not accepted by the installed version.
After the solver exits, inspect case_120.sta to determine whether the run terminated successfully by searching for the string JOB COMPLETED.
Capture the CalculiX version string by running ccx -v (or ccx --version, or equivalent) and record it verbatim.
Write a file named results.json in the working directory as a JSON object with the following fields: solver set to the string calculix, case_id set to case_120, status set to success if JOB COMPLETED appears in case_120.sta or to error otherwise, ccx_version set to the captured version string, artifacts set to a JSON array (empty if no notable artifacts are identified), and notes set to a string containing the exact ccx invocation command used plus, in the event of failure, the relevant error message and the filename from which the failure information was extracted.
